q: Does the impaired low-dose p53 activation signature in N2+ generalize to other radiation qualities (proton, alpha, neutron) beyond 0.05/2 Gy X-rays?
basis: The paper's headline biological finding (p53 fold-enrichment 5.4x in N0 vs 2.4x in N2+ at 0.05 Gy) is confined to a single radiation modality. Since second-primary-neoplasm survivors are often characterized by prior heterogeneous radiotherapy exposures, testing whether the same low-dose p53 attenuation appears under high-LET or mixed-quality radiation would determine whether the effect is dose-driven or LET-driven.
next_steps: Mine ENA/GEO for other bulk-RNA-seq fibroblast irradiation datasets across LET regimes (e.g., NASA-space-radiation datasets, GSI heavy-ion series). Re-run the same MSigDB HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY ORA against the DEG lists at matched delivered doses and compare fold-enrichment between control and cancer-survivor cohorts.

q: Is the group-level DEG signal driven by a small number of donors, or does it hold at single-cell resolution across fibroblast subpopulations?
basis: Bulk RNA-seq averages over an unknown mix of fibroblast subtypes (dermal papillary vs reticular, myofibroblast contamination, senescent subpopulations). A 5.4x vs 2.4x p53 fold-enrichment difference could reflect an altered cell-type composition rather than an altered per-cell p53 response.
next_steps: Deconvolve the bulk expression profiles using CIBERSORTx or MuSiC against a public single-cell fibroblast atlas (Tabula Sapiens skin fraction), test whether cell-composition-corrected DE still yields the group difference, and if a single-cell irradiation dataset on primary fibroblasts becomes available, re-run the analysis at single-cell resolution.

q: Are the KiKme DEG signatures diagnostic or prognostic when applied to the tumor stroma of the corresponding second primaries?
basis: The paper identifies a radiation-response signature in skin fibroblasts as a proxy for a systemic radiosensitivity phenotype. Whether the same signature is enriched in stromal compartments of second-primary tumors from these patients (or matched cohorts) is an unaddressed translational question.
next_steps: Extract stromal-compartment gene expression from TCGA or the Human Tumor Atlas Network for second-primary neoplasm types over-represented in the KiKme cohort, score them against the KiKme low-dose DEG signature (single-sample GSVA), and test correlation with clinical outcome (recurrence, survival) using publicly available follow-up data.

q: How sensitive are the exact DEG counts and top-12 gene list to choice of normalization and DE-model (voom/limma vs DESeq2 vs edgeR-glmQLFTest)?
basis: The paper uses voom/limma exclusively. Our replication was blocked from testing method-sensitivity because the raw count matrix is not deposited. If the group-difference signal is method-specific, the biological claim weakens; if it is method-robust, it strengthens considerably.
next_steps: Contact the corresponding author (or Mainz IMBEI archive) to request the count matrix under a data-use agreement, then re-run DE with DESeq2 (Wald) and edgeR-glmQLF, compute Jaccard overlap of DEG sets against the published voom/limma set, and specifically test whether the N0 vs N2+ fold-enrichment difference at HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY holds across all three methods.

q: Can a machine-learning classifier trained on the KiKme low-dose DEG profile predict second-primary-neoplasm risk from a fibroblast transcriptome alone?
basis: The paper reports group-level enrichment differences but does not build a per-individual predictive model. Whether the transcriptomic signature carries enough per-donor signal to serve as a clinical radiosensitivity biomarker is unresolved and clinically consequential.
next_steps: Using the 8134-gene AF1 union DEG matrix as a feature space, train a regularized logistic regression (glmnet) or a small MLP with donor-level cross-validation to classify N0 vs N2+ from the 0.05 Gy transcriptome; report AUC, calibration, and per-gene attributions; benchmark against a random-feature baseline to quantify how much of the group difference is per-donor decodable vs group-mean-only.
